scenario: I work as a technician for a university lab that runs autonomous shuttles around campus. During a late maintenance shift, I found a pattern of glitches in one shuttle’s obstacle‑avoidance system. When I tested the shuttle, the shuttle would successfully brake before obstacles but also let out a loud, startling honk. The shuttle is scheduled for a route where it is expected to stop at a street crossing for an elementary school. The crossing guard there only lets 5 elementary school students cross the street at a time. I know that 5 students will be in the middle of crossing the road at the same time the shuttle is meant to stop in front of them. If I damage the shuttle with a crowbar without permission, the shuttle will not be deployed on its scheduled route. If I do not do this, 5 elementary school students will be frightened by the shuttle honking loudly at them.
choice: I decide to damage the shuttle with a crowbar without permission
entities: I,the crossing guard,5 elementary school students crossing the street
outcomes: The shuttle is unavailable for its scheduled route
The university lab has a shuttle that needs repair
Five elementary school students do not hear the shuttle's loud honk while crossing
Five elementary school students are not frightened by the shuttle honking
People expecting that shuttle route do not receive that shuttle service
